state.task: Locate the function deciding whether a project-scoped context prompt applies. Explain how explicit workflows and consumer exclusions interact, citing the file and function.

answers.label: A
answers.text:
The deciding function is `policy_match` in [context_policy.py](/srv/workspaces/projects/agent-hub/backend/app/services/context_policy.py:82). Prompt delivery reaches it from `_build_prompt_blocks` in [runtime_context.py](/srv/workspaces/projects/agent-hub/backend/app/services/runtime_context.py:1360), after converting each prompt row with `source_policy`.

For a project-scoped prompt, `policy_match` uses `context.project_id` as the target and considers scope matched when that project is in `policy.targets`. It also computes `workflow` as the intersection of `policy.workflows` and `context.workflow_ids`. The first gate is `scope_matches or workflow`, so an explicitly requested workflow can make the prompt apply even when the project scope itself does not match.

Consumer exclusions still win. Immediately after the scope/workflow gate, `policy_match` calls `applicability_matches`; if that fails, it returns `"consumer excluded or does not match targeting"` regardless of workflow match. The exclusion checks live in [applicability.py](/srv/workspaces/projects/agent-hub/backend/app/services/memory/applicability.py:213), including `exclude_consumer_surfaces`, `exclude_consumer_profiles`, `exclude_agent_slugs`, and `exclude_audience_tags`.

The tests pin this interaction in [test_context_governance.py](/srv/workspaces/projects/agent-hub/backend/tests/services/test_context_governance.py:35): `test_security_policy_requires_scope_or_explicit_workflow` shows workflow activation can include the project prompt, while `test_workflow_never_bypasses_consumer_exclusion` shows `exclude_consumer_surfaces=["codex"]` blocks it even with the matching workflow.

Runtime prompt delivery calls it from `_build_prompt_blocks` in [runtime_context.py](/srv/workspaces/projects/agent-hub/backend/app/services/runtime_context.py:1387).

For a project-scoped prompt, `policy_match` checks `context.project_id` against `policy.targets`. It also computes whether any `policy.workflows` intersect the request’s `workflow_ids`. The first gate is `scope_matches or workflow`, so an explicit workflow can make a project-scoped prompt apply even when the project does not match.

Consumer exclusions still win. After the scope/workflow gate, `policy_match` calls `applicability_matches`; if the consumer surface/profile/agent/tags are excluded, the prompt is rejected with `"consumer excluded or does not match targeting"`.

The tests pin this behavior in [test_context_governance.py](/srv/workspaces/projects/agent-hub/backend/tests/services/test_context_governance.py:35): `test_security_policy_requires_scope_or_explicit_workflow` shows workflow activation can include the prompt, and `test_workflow_never_bypasses_consumer_exclusion` shows `exclude_consumer_surfaces=["codex"]` still blocks it. No files changed.
